newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi to prosecute police officers over jail death.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi to prosecute police officers over jail death.

text.p: Authorities in Hanoi said on Wednesday they were prosecuting two policemen following the death of a man in police custody in 1994.
An official at the People's Prosecutors Office said Nguyen Van Hoa and Ta Quang Vy would be charged with irresponsibility leading to serious consequences. No murder charges were mentioned.
Pham Thanh Quang died in Hanoi's Phuong Mai precinct police station on November 30, 1994, a few hours after being arrested. It was unclear on what charge he was detained.
Nguyen Van Hoa was a deputy head of the precinct at the time of the incident. The Prosecution office said both would face trial proceedings on November 16.
The Dai Doan Ket (Great Unity) newspaper quoted a prosecution indictment on Wednesday which described only light injuries to Pham Thanh Quang's face at the time he was brought to the police station.
"After his death there were many injuries to his body. Those injuries could not be caused by himself," the indictment said.
Vietnam nominated Ha Manh Tri of the National Assembly Law Committee as its new chief prosecutor on Monday.
In a speech to the assembly a few days before his nomination Tri called for tighter controls on the justice system to reduce false arrests and stop people being beaten while in custody.
"This is an important matter related to the democratic rights of citizens," he said, reading from a law committee report, adding: "...these cannot continue to be violated."

Though public trials of police officers are unusual in Vietnam, a Hanoi policeman was executed in March 1995 for murdering and robbing a 21-year-old motorcyclist who had been stopped for a traffic violation.
The case caused public outrage and police were forced to use tear gas to disperse thousands of people who gathered outside the Supreme Court building during the appeal hearing.
